title: Audit-log plain-language guidance for legal & procurement evaluations
body:
Purpose:
This is intended as a plain-language briefing and short script the legal/procurement teams and seller-facing reps can use when customers ask for audit-log evidence. It focuses on: (1) what our audit logs capture, (2) simple translations customers understand, (3) alignment to common requirements (SOC 2 / ISO / HIPAA), and (4) fast example artifacts we can provide in early diligence.

Audience and use-cases:
- Legal / procurement teams evaluating contract language and evidence requests.
- Sales engineering / CSEs needing one-liners and short examples to include in responses.
- Security reviewers who want a quick map from a requirement to our log fields.

Core messages (short/high-level):
- We produce immutable, timestamped audit logs that record control-relevant events across the inference lifecycle: authentication, model selection/deploy, request routing (region/pool), request/response metadata (no customer content unless requested), key management operations, and admin changes.
- Logs are retained per the contract/region; we provide exports to customer-controlled S3 or secure portal for agreed retention windows.
- Logs support common evidence workflows: timeline reconstruction, access review, anomaly detection, and cross-checks against billing/usage records.

Plain-language mappings (what reviewers ask vs. how we describe it):
- "Who accessed customer data?" -> "We log authenticated user/service identities with the action taken (e.g., inference request, config change), the timestamp, and the infrastructure node/region used. For Private deployments, logs can be routed to your SIEM or KMS-backed storage so only your tenants see them."
- "Was there a change to model weights or the serving config?" -> "We record deploy/change events (who initiated, what version/tag, delta summary) and keep a full version history for rollbacks and audit."
- "Can we reconcile billed tokens to requests?" -> "Each request has a request ID, model variant, token counts, and cost fields so our billing system can be reconciled to request-level logs."
- "Are logs tamper-evident?" -> "Write-once retention and HMAC checksums are applied to exported archives; internal logs include sequence numbers and audit trail metadata to make tampering detectable."

Minimum set of fields we will point to in evidence (simple catalog to attach to responses):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (UUID)
- principal_id (user/service)
- action (inference_request | deploy | config_change | auth_grant | key_rotation)
- model_id and model_version/tag
- region / cluster_id / node_id
- token_usage (prompt | generated | total)
- response_status (200 | 5xx | denied)
- admin_comment or change_summary (when applicable)

Quick sample audit-log line (plain text example you can paste):
2026-02-15T14:32:10Z | request_id=8f2b3c1e-92a4 | principal=svc-prod-ingest | action=inference_request | model=rw-13b-v0.9 | region=us-west1 | tokens={prompt:34, generated:84, total:118} | status=200

Recommended short seller scripts (one-liners and two-liners):
- For procurement review: "We provide signed, timestamped audit logs for control events (auth, deploys, inference requests) and can export them to your storage for independent ingestion into your SIEM. Retention and export format are contract configurable."
- For security teams: "Logs include request-level IDs, model/version, token counts for billing reconciliation, and HMAC-verified exports for tamper evidence. We keep a deployment history to show who changed serving configs and when."

Mapping to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / HIPAA checks (how to respond when they cite clauses):
- SOC 2 (CC6/CC7 related to change management & access): point to deploy & auth logs + version history. Attach a sample deploy-event stream and a short narrative on change approval workflows.
- ISO 27001 (A.12 / A.9): use the same mapping but emphasize export to customer SIEM and role-based access control logs for privileged operations.
- HIPAA (164.312 / access control & audit controls): provide the mapping that shows unique principal identifiers, action types, timestamps, and the ability to export logs for covered entity retention. Note: PHI content is not stored in logs unless the customer chooses to enable full request capture; by default we keep metadata only.

Competitive differentiators to call out in diligence: (short bullets for sales/legal)
- Customer-export-first: unlike some vendors that only offer portal access, we provide signed exports and SIEM-friendly formats (JSONL with documented schema) so customers can perform independent analysis.
- Reconciled billing artifacts: logs include token counts and cost fields to make financial and security reconciliation straightforward.
- Config and model lineage: not just "who accessed" but "which model version generated output" — important for explainability and regression analysis.

Fast artifacts we can attach (order these by low-effort -> higher-effort):
1) Redacted JSONL snippet (3 lines) showing request_id, timestamp, principal, model_version, and token counts.
2) High-level export manifest (checksums, date range) showing HMAC and export size.
3) Short deploy history (CSV) showing deploy author, tag, timestamp, and change summary for the last 30 days.
4) Sample SIEM mapping doc (one page) to show ingestion fields and example Splunk/Elastic query.

Common procurement/legal ask and suggested reply language (templates):
- Ask: "Provide 12 months of audit logs for review."
  Reply: "We can export X months of logs to your S3 bucket within the scope of the contracted export. Exports are delivered with checksums and an index file for rapid ingestion. For private deployments, retention is under your control and we can provide policy templates. See attached sample manifest."
- Ask: "Do logs contain customer content?"
  Reply: "By default logs capture metadata (IDs, timestamps, token counts, routing info). Full request/response capture (including content) is opt-in and subject to customer contract and governance. We recommend content capture only when necessary and under a Customer Data Agreement."

Risk & escalation notes (internal):
- If legal requests raw request content without DPA modifications, escalate to privacy/compliance — do not promise raw content in the reply.
- If a customer asks for real-time log streaming into their EDR/SIEM, confirm network architecture and Private/Dedicated deployment options with infra/solutions; this can create throughput and PII handling implications.

Open questions to resolve in next iteration (for product/security ops):
- Default export retention limits for hosted tier (we should state a sensible minimum in the next draft).
- Exact HMAC/signature format and where signing keys are stored (internal ops to confirm).
- Template wording for when customers request court/third-party subpoenas for logs (legal to draft).

Appendix: example redacted JSON log (3 line snippet you can paste into an RFP response)
{"timestamp":"2026-02-15T14:32:10Z","request_id":"8f2b3c1e-92a4","principal":"svc-prod-ingest","action":"inference_request","model":"rw-13b-v0.9","region":"us-west1","tokens":{"prompt":34,"generated":84,"total":118},"status":200}
{"timestamp":"2026-02-15T14:33:30Z","request_id":"9bb4a2f1-11c0","principal":"admin-console","action":"deploy","model":"rw-13b-v1.0","region":"us-west1","change_summary":"rolled back quantization config","status":200}
{"timestamp":"2026-02-16T02:05:00Z","request_id":"audit-archive-2026-02","principal":"system","action":"export","region":"us-west1","artifact":"s3://redwood-exports/customer-1234/2026-02-archive.jsonl","checksum":"sha256:abc123..."}
Last notes:
- Keep this doc as a quick reference for RFP/Security Q&A and ask product/security to review the open questions before we mark final.
- If you need a 1-page customer-facing artifact (lighter language), ask CSE content team and we will generate a PDF with the three sample artifacts above.

End of brief.
